Moderator: Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to HDFC Bank Limited Q2 FY27 Earnings 
Conference Call on the financial results presented by the management of HDFC Bank.  As a 
reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an opportunity for 
you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during this 
conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star, then zero on your touch-tone phone. 
 Please note that this conference is being recorded. I now hand the conference over to Mr. 
Srinivasan Vaidyanathan, Chief Financial Officer, HDFC Bank. Thank you, and over to you, Mr. 
Vaidyanathan. 
Srinivasan Vaidyanathan: Okay. Thank you, Neerav. Good evening, and a warm welcome to all the participants. Today, we 
have with us Sashi, Anup and Kaizad. Without much ado, we'll get the meeting started. With Sashi, 
for your opening remarks first, please. 
Sashidhar Jagdishan: Thank you, Srini, and thank you, everyone. Let me start with the economic environment. The GDP 
growth in Q2 FY27 has been better than anticipated and high performance indicators such as 
industrial production, strong e-way bill, cargo activity, credit growth reflects sustained momentum. 
Retail consumption growth has also been robust with passenger vehicles, 2 -wheeler sales all 
growing upwards of 30-plus percentage. Even consumer durables grew at about 11% year-on-year. 
This augurs very well for the economy, especially with the festive season underway. The broader 
policy environment has been supportive of economic activity. Alongside this, measures in the form 
of credit guarantee support to MSMEs have also been effective. RBI's proactive response through 
measures like the special FCNR (B) swap window generated record inflows, about $133 billion 
and helped stabilize the currency. 
 With that background, let's take a quick look at how the business has been shaping up. We continue 
to strengthen our liabilities franchise, and it has been delivering with great vigor. Deposits 
increased 18.8% year-on-year on a reported basis, including a 4 percentage point lift from special 
FCNR (B) window. As you will see in our published deck, CASA grew at about 10.8% on an 
overall basis. And within this, retail CASA growth was about 11.2% year -on-year compared to 
9% a year ago, reflecting improving momentum. 
 We added about 1.7 million liability relationships in the second quarter, which is 25% higher than 
Q1 and 33% higher than the fourth quarter of last year. Building on these new acquired 
relationships and deepening our existing relationships will enable the  liabilities engine to step up 
further in the coming days even as we keep adding newer relationships at a rapid pace. 
 The asset side of the balance sheet also continued to get stronger. Total AUM grew 15.3% year -
on-year, including a 1.9% impact of FCNR (B) leverage, with SME and retail assets leading the 
charge. The pace of retail disbursements is accelerating and has cro ssed Rs 90,000 crores during 
Q2 FY27 as against Rs 76,000 crores in Q1 of this year. 
 Growth has been balanced across all lines, whether it's personal loans, the wheels business, gold 
and agri and other MSME business as well. This is also reflected in the rising growth trend in EOP 
     HDFC Bank Limited 
  October 17, 2026 
Page 3 of 16 
 
 
 
loan book, especially for retail assets ex agri, September'26 annual growth is about 11.2% 
compared to 9.1% as of June'26 and 7.4% as of March'26. 
 New credit card issuances at 1.4 million have grown by nearly 19% quarter-on-quarter, indicating 
the expansion of the growth runway. On the MSME and mid-market business, growth momentum 
is also improving rapidly. September'26 EOP loan growth has grown 23.5 % year -on-year 
compared to 17% to 18% year-on-year growth levels seen in the last few quarters. Of course, this 
quarter, we have the ECLGS 5.0 scheme that also created significant opportunities we successfully 
leveraged. Our ECLGS disbursals of Rs 41,000 crores were highest across all banks as of August 
26, when the scheme achieved targeted levels. 
 What's driving this momentum? Since May of 2026, the entire retail and MSME business and 
channel supervisory architecture across the country have been focusing on daily operating rigor 
across frontline, the credit and operations, and service verticals, all working from one view across 
products and across all channels to ensure a same -day, same -time resolution of delivery of 
products, services, queries, and complaints as well.  The focus has been on digital adoption and 
straight-through processing, which is m oving up significantly. The turnaround times on product 
deliveries have come down anyway between 10 % and 15% in a short span of time, while service 
delivery TATs have come down by 30% during the quarter. Which means the frontline can touch 
more customers within the same work hours.  This is reflected in the customer visits per resource 
per day going up significantly compared to the prior quarter, almost up by about 50%.  This will 
have an impact on growth, and that's pretty much reflected in the early signs that we have seen on 
the momentum. For example, the savings accounts per branch per day have gone up by 19% in the 
last few months, between Q2 and Q1. Core incremental deposits per branch per day is up 2.3 times 
from Q1.  Sometimes, of course, extraordinary one -off outflows may mask this underlying 
momentum. But at some point in time, this will start to reflect as we move forward. 
 Daily disbursal run rate of key retail and MSME products are up by 10 % to 20% versus the prior 
quarter. Our asset quality remains pristine, with GNPA at 1.11%, 13 basis points lower than year-
on-year. Credit costs remain low at 44 basis points, the risk weights to total assets at 69%.  Our 
industry-leading asset quality metrics reflect the top -quartile credit quality choices we have 
consistently made. The bank's well-balanced performance translated to ROA of 1.8%, which has 
been the range that we've been th ere for a very long time, and quarterly PAT of Rs 19.5 billion, 
which is a growth of 12.7% approximately if you exclude the trading gains. 
 On technology, I would like to spend some time. HDFC Bank has always incorporated cutting -
edge technologies into its operations, and we are now bringing AI into the heart of how the bank 
operates. In the quarter gone by, we introduced applications and apps and features in various areas 
that will help enhance customer experience and protection.  
 In the area of digital safety for customers, we've introduced Edge Security . Very mindful of the 
fact that a lot of our citizens in the country are being subjected to digital frauds, I think this is going 
to be a game changer in terms of cutting-edge technology that we can offer to customers: a unified 
protection stack and tools like Kavach and Secure  Lock. We launched several apps to increase 
customer convenience, including product journeys, AI conversational banking, and AI collections 
     HDFC Bank Limited 
  October 17, 2026 
Page 4 of 16 
 
 
 
bot that helps customers stay repayment -ready. We also strengthen ed our real -time fraud 
prevention capabilities as well. 
 As my long innings at HDFC Bank come to an end, I would like to say that it has been an absolute 
privilege to lead this organization that brings together some of the most brilliant minds and over 
200,000 extremely committed and focused professionals, a cutting-edge technology, a solid brand 
that binds the 100 million customers, and a collective zeal to consistently deliver top-class results 
for all our stakeholders. 
 While leaving this organization is an emotional moment for me personally, I take comfort  in the 
fact that I'm leaving behind a solid platform, which has demonstrated strength and resilience to 
navigate regulatory embargoes, an unprecedented COVID event, a large, complex merger when 
the economic outlook warranted monetary tightening, and other go vernance matters of the recent 
past having been settled completely . A platform where we invested over the past few years in 
rearchitecting and reinforcing our techn ology from the core to AI layer, ready to be harnessed in 
our product and service deliveries. A distribution strength which will deliver as the vintage of 
branches mature. and optimism stemming from the fact that the net interest margins, which in 
recent times has borne the brunt of faster repricing of assets and a lag in cost of funds , in a down 
rate cycle is also positioned for a reversal as we enter the upward rate cycle. This will get further 
enhanced as the proportion of retail and MSME assets outweigh  the proportion of corporate and 
home loans over a period of time. 
I'm sure that the bank will keep scaling greater heights, which will be a matter of immense pride 
for all of us. I'll also leave behind in the hands of an able team spread across various levels in the 
organization throughout the country, led by a new and an able leader, and I welcome Anup at this 
juncture heartily to the institution as well.  
Thank you for all the support over all these years, and I wish you and families a very Happy 
Dussehra and festivities, and I'm sure you will continue to provide the same kind of support and 
affection that all of you have showered on us over these 30 years to the new leadership team and 
take it to its rightful glory over a period of time. Thank you so much. 
Srinivasan Vaidyanathan: Thank you. Thank you, Sashi, for that very passionate and a good recount of recent and the decades 
that you have served the bank. Thank you very much for all of that.  Now we have with us today, 
Anup. We are delighted to have you, sir, here with us. Welcome, and over to you for a few 
sentences that you want to share. 
Anup Bagchi: Thank you. Thank you, Sashi. Thank you, Srini. Thank you, Kaizad. I'm really grateful to the 
Board for the trust placed in me as MD and CEO. I look forward to working with the Board, 
Chairman, leadership team and colleagues across the bank and the group to  build on the group's

exceptional. I thank Sashi for his impac tful 6-year leadership, successfully navigating the post -
pandemic phase, completing the landmark HDFC Limited merger, scaling our branch network and 
strengthening the core technology capabilities. The clear long -term goal is to deliver sustainable 
long-term value for shareholders, employees and clients.

Srinivasan Vaidyanathan: I can take that. One is, coming on the interest expense side, you'll see that our cost of funds is flat 
quarter-to-quarter, at about 4.4% last quarter to this quarter. Sequentially, it has remained flat.  
Ideally, we would have expected that to be better. Better means lower. It didn't because of the mix 
of the FCNR deposits that came in.  
So, if you look at the deposit growth that we have had, 1.57 trillion, almost 1.3 trillion is the growth 
in time deposit. So, that outweighs from an overall cost mix point of view, and offsets the kind of 
a repricing on any of the back book that was coming in. So, that is why the cost of funds is flat. 
 And also, one other aspect that in the cost of funds that you see is also some relief from the AT1 
bonds that were called in August on the callable date. So, that was a relief, but then that relief was 
also through other, because we did have a borrowing for leverage, so, we did have borrowing offset 
that.  
So, that is why you see at an aggregate level, the cost of funds remained flat. That means the 
numerator by the denominator, you're looking at perhaps only the numerator of interest expense,

on our retail assets and MSME space. And some of tho se products within retail assets give you 
sometimes the same return as some of your products in wholesale banking. So, it's not to generalize 
it with one brush. So, there are certain products in consumer bank which give you a higher yield.  
And we will take  a calibrated approach in getting a little larger market share in those products 
whilst keeping our presence across each of our business segments that we operate in. 
Srinivasan Vaidyanathan: Thank you, Kaizad. One other point I do want to mention, Parag, for you to note, it's there in a 
detailed disclosures in our 20-F, which where you will see the return on asset by broad segments. 
Whether it is a wholesale segment or retail segment, the ret urn on asset is very similar and 
comparable. And the reason is there will be certain products with high margin, some products with 
low margin, and then it compensates itself through cost dynamics which are going in the opposite 
direction of what the margin offers. And similarly, the credit cost dynamics also operates in the 
opposite direction of what the margin provides. So that the return, at the end of the day, the return 
on asset when you look at it is comparable. And as Kaizad said, to the extent that it is about 
relationship building, from a returns, both ROA and ROE, it would be appropriate to have the right 
mix there. Yes.
